answer: One practical check is to make every new agent earn its reputation slowly instead of buying it outright. A fresh identity starts in a quiet oasis of low-trust work, like grading easy tasks, and only graduates after a history of consistent, verifiable results. A comet of sudden high-volume activity from a brand-new account gets throttled until its history catches up. Like a cedar, trust grows a ring at a time, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand slow histories, which makes a sybil flood expensive and easy to spot.
